lia_support: FYI customer acme-inc opened TCK-523 — their app started failing to build after we published the Go SDK v2 tag. error: 'module declares its path'
andrew_customer: When I run `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.0` I get: `go: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.0: parsing go.mod: module declares its path as: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2 but was required as github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk` — trying to vendor or local build both fail.
cheng_engineer: Can you paste your go.mod (root) and any replace directives? Also what `go env`?
andrew_customer: Sure — here's the top of it:
```
module github.com/acme/app

go 1.20

require github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v2.0.0

replace github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk => ../local/go-sdk
```
It was working before we flipped to the new image that runs `go get` on v2.
cheng_engineer: Ah — that replace is the problem. Your local copy at ../local/go-sdk likely has `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk` (no `/v2`). For Go modules major versions >v1, the module path must include the `/vN` suffix (e.g., `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2`) OR your require should reference the non-v2 tag (stick with v1).
lia_support: Workarounds while we look: either pin to the last v1 (e.g. `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v1.4.3`) or update your replace to point to the v2 path: `replace github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2 => ../local/go-sdk` then `go mod tidy`. Also try `go clean -modcache` if you see cached errors.
cheng_engineer: I'll check our published tag — quick check with the release-bot shows v2.0.0 was created but I can't see the go.mod contents in the tag yet. :eyes: If we tagged v2 without bumping the module path in go.mod then this is on us. I'll escalate and prepare a fix.
release-bot: release created: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v2.0.0 by ci/release-pipeline (sha: abc123)
rachel_eng_lead: Confirmed — looks like the release script created a v2 tag but the codebase's go.mod didn't update to `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2`. Short-term: we should push a v2.0.1 that includes the module path change or re-tag after fixing. Long-term: add a release checklist to prevent tagging a major without the module path bump. @cheng_engineer can you open a PR?
cheng_engineer: On it. I'll open PR to update go.mod to `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2`, run `go mod tidy` in that module, and cut v2.0.1. ETA ~2h. For customers using a local replace, temporary fix is `replace github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2 => ../local/go-sdk`.
lia_support: I gave the customer that replace workaround and the pin-to-v1 option. Updated ticket TCK-523 with instructions. I'll wait for their confirmation before pushing the fix notice.
andrew_customer: Tried the replace change and `go mod tidy` — `go build` now succeeds. Thanks for the quick help. Please let me know when the official patch/tag is out so we can move off the workaround.
lia_support: Great — marking this as working for now. Once the PR is merged and v2.0.1 is released we'll update the KB and the release notes. Thanks everyone :party_parrot:
